 Print Floyd Mayweather’s bid to break Hopkins’ record faces medical and licensing conditions Floyd Mayweather could get a chance to become boxing’s oldest world champion if a proposed fight with Ryan Garcia goes ahead in 2027. World Boxing Council president Mauricio Sulaiman says the rules would allow the 49-year-old to challenge for Garcia’s welterweight title, but only if he passes medical checks and holds a valid boxing license. Garcia has named February 6 in Las Vegas for the fight and says it would be a professional contest, not an exhibition. However, neither camp has formally confirmed the full fight details or whether Garcia’s title will be at stake. Mauricio Sulaiman Says Floyd Mayweather Can Challenge for Ryan Garcia’s WBC Title 
 Sulaiman discussed the possible fight with Fight Hub TV at the WBC convention in Acapulco, Mexico. He said Garcia had already met his mandatory challenger, Conor Benn. That means Garcia can choose his next opponent for a voluntary title defense. The WBC president did not promise that the fight would happen. Mayweather would first need to pass medical checks and hold a valid boxing license. Sulaiman also pointed to past comebacks by older boxers. Some did not go well, including Mike Tyson’s 2024 loss to Jake Paul. But he named Manny Pacquiao and Sergio Martinez as examples of fighters who returned and remained competitive. Pacquiao, then 46, faced WBC welterweight champion Mario Barrios in July 2025. The fight ended in a draw. Mayweather would be trying to pass Bernard Hopkins’ mark as the oldest male world champion. Guinness World Records lists Hopkins as the record holder after he beat Beibut Shumenov on April 19, 2014, at 49 years and 94 days. Mayweather would be 49 if he fought Garcia on February 6, 2027. A world title win would put him beyond that mark. Ryan Garcia Names February Date as Floyd Mayweather Faces Legal Questions
 Garcia spoke about the proposed fight during a livestream. He said the two would meet on February 6 in Las Vegas and made clear that he wanted a professional bout. “We have an announcement,” Garcia said. “We are going to fight Floyd Mayweather on February 6. Floyd, we’re going to kick your a**. This is not an exhibition. This is a real fight. I’m going to take his zero.” Mayweather has not released a full fight announcement with the venue, broadcaster or official terms. He did post about an exhibition against Australian boxer Matt “The Jedi” Floyd, scheduled for December 19 in Bangkok. Mayweather called it a tune-up before a possible Garcia fight in February 2027. There is also a legal issue. CSI Sports sued Mayweather in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, claiming he broke an agreement by taking other fights. In July, the judge denied the company’s request for an emergency order to stop him. CSI later withdrew its request for a preliminary injunction in August. The contract case remained active in the court docket last updated on August 10. Join conversation

 The July decision did not settle the dispute. Garcia’s legal adviser, Guadalupe Valencia, told Ring Magazine’s Mike Coppinger: “When Floyd is free from other obligations, we will certainly work to make this fight happen; hopefully, real soon. This would only be a real fight—not an exhibition—with Mayweather’s 50-0 on the line.” Garcia has also spoken about facing WBA welterweight champion Teofimo Lopez. For now, the Mayweather fight remains a proposal. The WBC’s position means its rules do not automatically prevent Mayweather from challenging, but medical clearance, a license and agreement between the camps are still needed.
